title: One Shared Secret Opens the Same Claude Door | vitalii.no
description:
How a Claude proxy built for a single browser-based app learned to trust a second, server-only app too — without giving up its original login.

The Claude proxy on ghost.vitalii.no only accepted a Google user's bearer token, because it was built for one interviewer app talking to one browser. When a separate, browser-less Cloudflare Worker project needed to ask the same proxy a question, it had no user and no login to show — the only options were running its own paid API key or duplicating the entire authorization flow just to get through the door.

The fix adds an internal-key check inside the proxy's authorization function, running before the existing Google-token path. It reads a custom header and compares it against a shared secret one character at a time in constant time, accumulating any difference with XOR instead of exiting early, so a wrong guess can't leak timing information back to an attacker. If the header matches, the request skips the Google check entirely; if it's missing or wrong, the original login path still runs exactly as before.

The second project can now call the shared endpoint directly with its own key, and the original Google-authenticated flow keeps working unchanged — one door, two valid ways in.
